text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like NVDA on 2026-09-18, the median realised return over the next 5 sessions was 0.86%. The distribution is wide and slightly right-skewed, with a standard deviation of 3.8%, meaning the single number to anchor on is that median 0.86% rather than the mean of 0.65%, as the path frequently swings far in both directions before settling.

[state]
The engine selected these analogs because the current state combines several distinctive features. NVDA is sitting -6.03% from its 52-week high (z-score 0.564) after a 60-session return of 11.82% (z-score 0.39). Its own 20-session realised volatility is elevated at 45.77% (z-score 0.824), while the benchmark 20-session volatility is unusually quiet at 9.16% (z-score -0.574). A major macro driver pulling specific episodes into this neighborhood is the WTI crude change over 20 days at 19.24% (z-score 1.124), the most extreme feature in the set. Additionally, the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score is negative at -0.785 (used as -0.62), and there are 45 calendar days to the next earnings release (z-score 0.663) with 0 scheduled events in the next 5 sessions (z-score -0.496). These weights—30% name-level price/vol features, 20% market, 20% macro, 10% crypto, and 20% event—pulled 50 analogs across 31 distinct sessions and 33 distinct symbols, dominated by Technology (9), Health Care (5), Financials (5), and Energy (4) names.

[history]
Over the 5-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced a median return of 0.86% and a mean of 0.65%, with outcomes ranging from -7.34% to 10.25%. The distribution is slightly right-skewed (skew 0.214): 56% of episodes finished above 0%, while 44% finished below. The 10th percentile sits at -4.04% and the 90th at 4.68%. The bad tail is heavily influenced by two specific episodes. The closest match is NVDA itself on 2026-09-08 (distance 0.2999), which returned -5.9% over the following week. Another drag on the left tail is XLK on 2026-08-13 (distance 0.4178), which returned -4.02%. Conversely, the best outcome came from another NVDA episode on 2025-06-20 (distance 0.4317), which rallied 9.66%. The conformal interval, scaled at 1.31 and fitted on 2019-2022 data, spans from -4.12% to 5.83% (width 9.95%), achieving 80.8% out-of-sample coverage on 2698 test queries.

[tails]
A position can end near the median and still be un-holdable through the week. Across the 50 analogs, the median max adverse excursion was -2.01%, meaning the typical path dipped roughly twice as deep as it ultimately closed. The 10th percentile of max adverse excursion reached -4.38%, and the 25th percentile was -3.77%. In terms of drawdown breaches during the 5 sessions, 8% of the analog paths breached a 5% drawdown at some point. Zero episodes out of the 50 breached a 10%, 15%, or 20% drawdown intraweek. On the upside, the median max favourable excursion was 2.55%, with the 75th percentile reaching 4.39% and the 90th percentile hitting 6.71%. This yields a historical reward-to-risk ratio of 1.27 based on the excursion medians.

[stress]
When conditioned on severe historical regimes, the baseline picture deteriorates materially in several cases. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario (48 analogs) is the most punishing: the median forward return drops to -5.4% (a delta of -6.26% versus baseline), the 10th percentile hits -14.14%, and 58.3% of paths breached a 10% drawdown. However, central-bank backstops arrived inside that window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns; it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast of the next one. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare (50 analogs) produces a median of -3.02% (delta -3.88%) and a 10th percentile of -6.18%, but it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs. The 2022 inflation/rate bear (50 analogs) shows a median of -2.42% (delta -3.28%) and a 10th percentile of -8.44%; because it is a nine-month window sampled repeatedly with a per-date cap of 2 analogs, treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind (36 analogs) yields a median of -2.11% (delta -2.97%) and a 10th percentile of -8.61%, though the reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not. The 2025-04 tariff shock (26 analogs) gives a median of -2.7% (delta -3.56%) and a 10th percentile of -8.21%, but policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The volatility spike scenario (50 analogs) results in a median of -0.18% (delta -1.04%) and a 10th percentile of -7.47%; VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, so this stresses entry timing more than terminal value. The liquidity air pocket scenario (50 analogs) shows a median of 0.83% (delta -0.03%) and a 10th percentile of -6.64%. Crucially, gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, not on a 7x24 venue. Measured on the wrapper itself (NVDAG_USDT, Gate.io spot v4), the reference market is closed for 81.4% of the week and 54.31% of the wrapper's realised hourly movement happened in those closed hours, so the gap risk this scenario describes is not hypothetical for the instrument a trader would hold. Milder scenarios include the 2023-03 regional bank stress (median 1.51%, delta 0.65%; caveat: very short window, analog set dominated by a handful of sessions), earnings release day (median 1.61%, delta 0.75%; caveat: foreign private issuer dates from 6-K full-text search are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates), FOMC decision day (median 0.07%, delta -0.79%; caveat: only 92 decision days exist, so the analog set is small and highly overlapping), policy-rate path re-pricing (median -0.39%, delta -1.25%; caveat: uses DGS3MO/T10Y2Y levels as proxies, transmission depends on duration/balance sheet not featured here), crypto drawdown contagion (median 0.8%, delta -0.06%; caveat: BTC feature is a market-wide proxy, name-level linkage not identified, fng excluded from distance), and China ADR de-rating (median -0.06%, delta -0.92%; caveat: delisting and audit-access risks are structural and will not appear in a price/vol feature space). No scenarios were skipped.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The engine's own validation states explicitly: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." At matched coverage, the analog method is -7.6% less sharp than the same-name unconditional benchmark. The directional hit rate is 50.1%. The dataset spans 2513 sessions across 71 symbols from 2016-09-20 to 2026-09-18, using prices from api.stockanalysis.com and earnings from SEC full-text search clustered at 6 calendar days. Regarding execution, the tokenised wrapper NVDAG_USDT on Gate.io spot v4 has a status of "measured" and is classified as a "fair tracker". It carries a return correlation of 0.8971 and a tracking error of 114 bp/day over 55 overlapping sessions. The reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week (136.67 hours), and 54.31% of the wrapper's own realised hourly price movement landed in those shut hours. The wrapper trades at a premium band of -0.44% to 0.65% over the underlying's last raw close of 222.27, with a current spread of 13.54 bps. As the card notes, a fair tracker is not the underlying—at 114 bp/day of tracking error the wrapper carries its own idiosyncratic risk, and the premium band means the exit price can differ from the reference close the analog distribution is built on. This measurement was taken on Gate.io spot v4, not a Bitget feed, and nothing from the wrapper feeds the retrieval engine or conformal scale.
